stem: What is a prototype?

options.content: An early working model that users can try
The final system after it has been fully tested
options.rationale: A prototype is an early model.

options.content: A document listing the user requirements
A back-up copy of the system
options.rationale: A prototype is not a backup.

explanation: A prototype is an early model used to find out what the users need.

stem: What happens to a prototype in throwaway prototyping?

options.content: It is thrown away after use
It is developed into the final system
It is sold to the users as the final system
options.rationale: A throwaway prototype is not delivered.

options.content: It is used as the user guide

explanation: Throwaway prototypes are built to learn the requirements and then discarded.

stem: Which is a benefit of prototyping?

options.content: The users do not need to be involved
Users see a working version early, so problems show up early
The project always finishes sooner than a waterfall project
options.rationale: Prototyping can continue for too long.

options.content: No documentation is needed

explanation: Early feedback is the main benefit of prototyping.

stem: In object-oriented methodology, what is a class?

options.content: One particular object, such as the learner Tendai Moyo
options.rationale: That is an instance (object) of a class.

options.content: A group of users who test the system
options.rationale: That is not an OOM term.

options.content: A template for the attributes and methods of objects
The language used to write the system
options.rationale: A class is not a language.

explanation: A class is the template; an object is one instance of it.

stem: In a hospital system the classes Doctor and Nurse both have the attributes name and staff number. How can the duplication be removed?

options.content: Delete the shared attributes from both of the classes
Make Doctor and Nurse objects of each other's classes
options.rationale: Classes are not objects of each other.

options.content: Store the shared attributes in a data flow diagram
options.rationale: A diagram does not hold data.

options.content: Make a Staff class that Doctor and Nurse inherit from

explanation: A parent class holds the shared attributes and the subclasses inherit them.
hints: Where can shared attributes be defined once?

stem: A company wants a new payroll system. The requirements are fixed by law and will not change. Which process model is the most suitable?

options.content: Throwaway prototyping, because the users are unsure
options.rationale: The requirements are fixed, so there is little to discover.

options.content: Waterfall
options.rationale: Correct: stable requirements suit a sequence of stages.

options.content: Evolutionary prototyping, because the rules change daily
No model, because payroll is simple

explanation: Stable, well-understood requirements suit the waterfall model.

stem: A student reads "The clinic keeps a record of each patient and each appointment" and decides that `Patient` and `Appointment` are classes. Which technique did the student use?

options.content: Picking out the verbs, which suggest classes
Drawing a flowchart
Picking out the nouns in the description
Running a prototype

explanation: Nouns suggest classes and verbs suggest methods.
hints: Which kind of word is Patient?

stem: Which of these is a drawback of evolutionary prototyping?

options.content: The users never see the system until the very end
The prototype is always thrown away
It cannot be used with changing requirements
options.rationale: It is designed for changing requirements.

options.content: The system may be untidy and hard to maintain

explanation: Many quick changes can lead to a messy design.
hints: What happens to a design that is changed many times?

stem: An object is one instance of a class.
explanation: True. The class is the template and the object is a particular example.

stem: In inheritance, a subclass can use the attributes and methods of its parent class.
explanation: True. This avoids writing the same attributes and methods again.

stem: Match each object-oriented term to its meaning.

right.content: A piece of data held by an object
An action that an object can carry out
A class takes over the attributes and methods of a parent class
A template for a kind of object

explanation: These are the basic terms of object-oriented methodology.

stem: Match each type of prototyping to its description.

right.content: Built after the final system as a back-up
Built to learn the requirements and then discarded
Refined after each review until it becomes the final system

explanation: Throwaway is discarded; evolutionary becomes the system.

stem: Complete the sentences.

payload.template: In OOM the nouns in the description suggest {{blank:a}} and the verbs suggest {{blank:b}}.

explanation: Nouns suggest classes; verbs suggest methods.

stem: Name the object-oriented feature that allows a class to take over the attributes and methods of another class.
explanation: Inheritance.
The seats of the two buses and the taxi add up to 112.
hints: Add the seats of the three vehicles.

stem: A class `Vehicle` defines 2 attributes (`registration` and `seats`). Its subclass `Bus` adds 1 attribute (`route`) and its subclass `Taxi` adds none, because they inherit the attributes of `Vehicle`. Without inheritance each class would define all of its own attributes, so `Bus` would define 3 and `Taxi` 2. How many fewer attribute definitions are needed with inheritance than without it?
hints: Count how many attributes are defined in each class.

stem: Discuss the benefits and drawbacks of prototyping. [4]

points.description: Benefit: the users see a working version early, so misunderstandings are found early
Benefit: the users take part, so they are more likely to accept the final system
Drawback: the users may think the prototype is nearly the whole system (or a rushed prototype has a poor design)
Drawback: the project may continue too long because users keep asking for changes

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Users see a working version early so misunderstandings are found early, and they take part, so they are more likely to accept the final system. However users may think the prototype is nearly finished, and the project can continue for too long as they ask for more changes.

explanation: Two benefits with reasons and two drawbacks.

stem: A school library records books, members and loans. Identify three classes, and give one attribute and one method for each. [4]

points.description: Book class with an attribute such as title
Member class with an attribute such as name
Loan class with an attribute such as date due
A suitable method for each class, for example borrow, return or calculateFine

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Book (title; method: markAsBorrowed), Member (name; method: borrowBook) and Loan (date due; method: calculateFine).

explanation: Classes come from nouns; methods from verbs.

stem: A cooperative in Mutare wants a mobile app for its farmers. The farmers have never used such an app and cannot say exactly what they want. Recommend a process model and justify your choice. [4]

points.description: Recommends prototyping
The requirements are unclear, so the farmers need to see something working to say what they want
Each prototype gives feedback that is used to improve the next one
The waterfall model would deliver a system that may not meet their needs, found out only at the end

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Prototyping is suitable. The farmers cannot say what they want until they see something working, and each prototype gives feedback that improves the next one. With the waterfall model the mismatch would only be found at the end.

explanation: Recommendation with reasons from the scenario.
hints: Name the model, link it to the scenario and give a reason.

stem: Explain how object-oriented methodology allows software to be reused. [3]

points.description: Each class is a self-contained template with its own data and methods
A class written for one project can be used again in another project
Subclasses can inherit and extend a tested class instead of writing everything again

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Each class is self-contained, so a class from one project can be used again in another, and a subclass can inherit and extend a tested class instead of writing everything again.

explanation: Self-contained classes and inheritance.

stem:
A transport company uses these classes.

| Class | Attributes | Methods | Parent |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| Vehicle | registration, seats | summary | none |
| Bus | route | summary (overrides) | Vehicle |
| Taxi | none of its own | none of its own | Vehicle |

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Name the attribute that is defined in `Bus` but not in `Vehicle`.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: How many attributes does a `Taxi` object have?

options.rationale: Inherited attributes are still attributes of the object.
Correct: registration and seats are inherited from Vehicle.
Taxi does not have the route attribute.

parts.explanation: A Taxi object has the 2 inherited attributes.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain how inheritance helps the developer in this design.

points.description: The attributes registration and seats are written once, in Vehicle
Bus and Taxi use them without repeating the definitions
A change to a shared attribute is made in one place

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The shared attributes are written once, in Vehicle. Bus and Taxi use them without repeating the definitions, and a change is made in one place.

explanation: Taxi inherits everything from Vehicle; Bus adds a route and overrides summary.

stem: A college in Chinhoyi will develop an online enrolment system. The registrar is not sure what screens are needed. The college expects to add fee payment and accommodation later, and wants to reuse parts of the system. Prototyping would take 15 weeks in 5 prototypes of 3 weeks each.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: How many weeks would prototyping take?

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain why prototyping is suitable for this project.

points.description: The registrar is unsure what screens are needed
She can try each prototype and say what to change
The final system is therefore closer to what is needed

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The registrar is unsure what screens are needed, so she can try each prototype and say what to change, and the final system is closer to what is needed.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why an object-oriented approach is suitable for this project.

points.description: Fee payment and accommodation can be added later as new classes
Classes such as Student can be reused by the new parts
A change is limited to one class

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: New parts such as fee payment and accommodation can be added later as new classes, classes such as Student can be reused, and a change is limited to one class.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State one reason why the waterfall model would be less suitable.

points.description: The requirements are unclear and would not be known at the start

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The requirements are unclear and would not be known at the start.

explanation: Prototyping suits unclear requirements; OOM suits a system that will be extended; waterfall suits fixed requirements.
hints: Match the project to the characteristics of each model.
